findings.title: Cleanup now runs ten times as often
findings.body: Changing the ticker from 10 minutes to 1 minute causes every cleanup job to run up to ten times as often, although this PR only changes annotation cleanup. That increases recurring database and filesystem work in production and can create unnecessary load; preserve the existing interval unless the increased frequency is intentional and justified.

findings.title: Building SQLite ID lists repeatedly copies the growing string
findings.body: This loop uses `fmt.Sprintf` to append each ID to an immutable string, copying the entire accumulated list on every iteration. With the supported large SQLite batch sizes (the new test uses 32,767), this produces quadratic copying and can consume substantial CPU and memory during cleanup. Build the list with a `strings.Builder` or another linear-time approach.

findings.title: Successful cleanup batches are logged as errors
findings.body: This log call uses error severity for routine cleanup progress, and the same pattern is used for the other cleanup batches below. Every cleanup run can therefore emit error-level records even when no operation failed, including the selected IDs and query condition. This pollutes error monitoring and can generate large log volumes; use an appropriate non-error level and log IDs only when needed.
